newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Korean kangaroo yields rise on rating warnings.
newsitem.headline: Korean kangaroo yields rise on rating warnings.

text.p: There is a growing unease by investors about Asian debt securities in the Australian market following last week's decision by U.S. credit rating agencies to put some South Korean banks on review for a possible downgrade.

Two of them, Korea Long-Term Credit Bank and Korea Exchange Bank, both issued debt in Australia's budding kangaroo market for a total A$305 million last year and the rating news caused their yields to rise initially.
Korea Development Bank, which issued the first ever bonds under a kangaroo structure has escaped review, but still had its credit outlook revised to negative from stable by Moody's.
However, the plight of the Korean banks is not seen having immediate implications for the wider kangaroo market.
These instruments are debt raising by foreign issuers in the Australian domestic bond market.
Moody's said that its action reflected the continued deterioration in the asset quality of the principal banks in Korea, which continues to undermine their capital position and their core earnings.

Jason Carley, Head of Reseach at ANZ Investment Bank, said the outlook for the Korean banking sector was under a cloud until a clearer picture emerges of the state of South Korea's industrial sector and suggested investors take a cautious approach towards the banks over the next few months.
He also believes that the current currency crisis in the Asian region is a concern and could have wider implications for the kangaroo bond market.
"Asian companies at present are 'do-able' in the kangaroo market," Carley said. "But a lot of work by lead managers would be needed."
Other kangaroo bonds, however, have not been effected.
Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, which has visited the kangaroo market twice this year for a total of A$350 million, has experienced strong investor demand on both occasions.
A Merrill Lynch official told Reuters that he did not see the potential downgrade of Korean banks as a limiting factor on the growth of the kangaroo bond market.
"The growth of the kangaroo market will be based on the quality of issuers," he said. "We expect the kangaroo market to continue to grow in the domestic market."
